name: The grain road (south and west toward Andorhal)
region: Lordaeron, from the sick village south and west past the ford

sensoryProfile.sight: A rutted road between hedges, 'rutted deep by every loaded cart that had ever come up it'; at the bottom of the village, past the brook, the road splits: north back toward Millhaven, south and west the grain road.
sensoryProfile.touch: The staff in Jaina's arm leans on its own toward the ruts.
sensoryProfile.atmosphere: The road the young man's cart came by; the party leaves in the order of the crest.

establishedFacts.fact: Andorhal is 'the big granaries. Down the grain road, south and west, past the ford. Three days, with a cart. Everything in the south goes through Andorhal, one way or another.' (Brask)
A ford lies on the road; Joss's flour cart was sent there that morning for the Hallams and the alehouse; Dickon caught it and turned it round.

eventsHere.event: The party turns onto the grain road at the end of chapter 4, following the young man with the cart.

Chapter 5: the road crosses a ford at noon (the party crosses it); beyond it the hedges fall back to stubble and the road runs straight and wide, 'built for carts', to Corley's depot at a crossroads. Dawn rain had filled the ruts; the ruts are deep enough that a horse who stepped wrong would go in to the knee. The grain-road trail then fans into four roads from the depot.
